description:
**The headline feature is at 10% coverage and the machinery to fix it shipped weeks ago.**

praxis constructs GATED notebook tutorials — AI-built knowledge checks that gate progression are the product. `python -m praxis.coverage` reports **24 of 245** notebooks gated, with **6 of 14 domains at 0%**: symbolic-AI/logic, agentic-AI, speech-audio, proprietary-coding-AI, procedural-generation, and data-analysis/research. Only 24 notebooks carry `nbgrader` metadata and there are 24 `.checks.json` sidecars.

`79-gating-backfill-by-domain` shipped the batch RUNNER — `backfill.py`, `coverage.py`, `regate.py`, `gateaudit.py` all merged. The batches never ran. An 18-repo audit on 2026-08-25 found no tasklist owning the run itself, in any repo.

**This is compute and review time, not code**, which is exactly why it slipped: every tasklist in the program had an obvious code deliverable and this one does not. It is also why the repo shows zero active tasklists and reads as finished — the 10→60 program did complete, and then the thing the program was for was left at a tenth of its scope.

**Quality is the risk, not throughput.** Generating 221 notebooks' worth of knowledge checks is cheap; generating 221 notebooks' worth of checks that actually gate — that a learner cannot pass without understanding the material, and that do not fabricate content the notebook never taught — is the work. The repo already has `gateaudit.py` for this. A backfill that raises coverage while lowering gate quality is a worse outcome than 24 good ones.

userStories.title: A domain is backfilled end to end, and its gates are audited
acceptanceCriteria: One zero-coverage domain is taken from 0% to complete using the shipped runner. Pick the domain that best exercises the machinery rather than the smallest one — the point is to learn what the runner does badly before committing to 221 notebooks.

Every generated gate passes `gateaudit.py`. A gate that a learner can pass without engaging the material is not coverage, and raising the coverage number while lowering gate quality is a worse outcome than the current 24.
Whatever the runner gets wrong is FIXED in the runner, not hand-patched in the output. That is the difference between this run and a one-off.
The per-notebook cost is recorded — wall time, tokens, and how much human review each needed. That figure is what makes the remaining scope a decision rather than a guess.
userStories.notes: praxis.authored run 01-symbolic-ai-logic: 15 of 15 topics gated in 47.1s (3.1s per notebook), 90 checks (45 choice, 31 short, 14 code). python3 -m praxis.gateaudit notebooks/01-symbolic-ai-logic: audited 15 gates (90 checks), 0 flagged; whole library python3 -m praxis.gateaudit: 39 gates (234 checks), 0 flagged; python3 -m praxis.regate: 39 gates, 39 hold, 0 flagged. python3 -m praxis.coverage: Symbolic Ai Logic 15/15 100%, library 39/245 (16%) in 9 of 14 domains, up from 24/245 in 8. Gate green: scripts/validate_nbgrader.py notebooks -> 39 notebooks, 0 failures; python3 -m pytest -q tests/ -> 1161 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (378s); node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs --ratchet -> 0 dead vs 0 on main. Domain chosen to exercise the machinery, not to be cheap: 14 runnable topics that must carry a code check plus one conceptual topic that must carry none. Runner defect found and FIXED IN THE RUNNER: backfill_domain -> construct_each -> generate_checks is a grader wrapped around one HTTP call, so with no provider configured the grading was unreachable too — which is why the shipped batches sat unrun. praxis/authored.py supplies the asking half from disk; every downstream refusal (checkset_failures verify_code=True, the gateaudit triviality rules, publish_graded_cells, nbgrader validate) runs unchanged, and 11 tests in tests/test_authored.py pin each refusal against a file rather than a model. Three suite tests pinned the shipped 24-gate corpus by exact count and failed BECAUSE coverage rose; now a floor plus the property, selecting by state not position. Cost recorded in docs/explanation/gating-backfill-cost.md: machine time 3.1s/notebook (4 subprocess launches per runnable notebook), authoring ~15.4kB of prose read and ~10.5kB of gate written per notebook, and 2 of 15 drafts rejected by the write path on their first pass (a code check whose reference solution failed its own test; an unsound all-different propagation rule) — both caught by the machine, one repair round each, zero human-only findings.

userStories.title: The remaining domains are run, or the scope is deliberately cut
acceptanceCriteria: The remaining zero-coverage domains are backfilled, OR a reasoned decision cuts the scope — with the cut recorded. If US-1's measured cost makes 221 notebooks unreasonable, saying so and gating a chosen subset is a legitimate outcome; silently leaving it at 10% is not.
Coverage after the run is reported by `praxis.coverage`, per domain, so the claim is checkable.
Notebooks deliberately left ungated are marked as such with a reason, so ungated-by-choice is distinguishable from ungated-by-omission. That distinction does not exist today.
`gateaudit.py` passes across the whole gated set, not only the newly generated part — a backfill that regresses existing gates has not helped.

userStories.title: Coverage stops being discoverable only by audit
acceptanceCriteria: Gate coverage is reported somewhere a reader meets it — the README's product claim, or the gate — rather than only from `python -m praxis.coverage`. The current figure was found by running a command nobody had run.

The ROADMAP's gating-backfill row records what actually happened: the machinery merged, the batches ran (or were cut), and where coverage landed. It currently describes the pre-state as though the code had not shipped.
A regression check fails if coverage drops, so this cannot silently decay back. Cheap and offline; it is a count over sidecars, not a model call.
